concerns.text: Task T003 is tagged `[P]` (parallel‑safe) but it writes to the shared state file `state/projects/PROJ-230-evaluating-the-effectiveness-of-prompt-e.yaml`. Later task T018 also writes to the same file. Parallel execution could cause race conditions, so the `[P]` tag is unsafe.

User‑Story 2 (tasks T002, T007‑T011) cannot be shipped independently because it depends on artifacts produced in US 1 (the processed corpus from T005). Each US block must be independently testable end‑to‑end, which is violated here.

User‑Story 3 (tasks T012‑T014) also depends on artifacts from earlier stories (corpus, generated JavaScript). This cross‑story dependency breaks the requirement that each US block be independently shippable.

Task T009 consumes generated JavaScript files, but no prior task explicitly produces those files. Task T008 describes inference but does not state that it writes the `.js` outputs; therefore T009 has a consumer‑before‑producer ordering violation.
